name: DFRobot FireBeetle 2 ESP32-C5 (ESP32-C5-WROOM-1-N4)
radio: the SoC's own radios: wifi24, wifi5, ble, ieee802154

flash.bootloader_instructions: Hold BOOT (GPIO28) while plugging in USB-C, or hold BOOT and tap RST; release after a second. The chip's USB-JTAG-serial port appears.
flash.note: CircuitPython's downloadable .bin is a merged image (bootloader, partition table and app at their own offsets inside it) and is written at 0x0 on every Espressif chip, as Adafruit's web flasher does; the C5's bootloader address of 0x2000 is already inside the image. To be confirmed with the first board.

usb.when: ESP32-S3/C5 USB-JTAG-serial (download mode and, with CDC on boot, the running firmware)

pins.name: IO15
pins.note: onboard LED; IO15 in the DevKitC-1 CircuitPython build's pin names

battery.divider_note: Powered from USB or a 5 V pack. A pack with a low-current auto-off cuts power while the fox sleeps (schedule.sleep deep), and the board never wakes; use one without.

notes: A variant of the ESP32-C5 chip target: it runs the same CircuitPython build as the XIAO ESP32-C5 (espressif_esp32c5_devkitc_1_n8r8); the Board dropdown on the Radio & pins tab picks this board's LED pin.
Serial: native USB CDC (no bridge chip); Listen only shows the ROM banner and the fox's lines.
Power: a network fox with schedule.sleep deep sleeps between wakes; a USB power bank with a low-current auto-off cuts power during the sleep and the fox never wakes. Use a pack without auto-off.
Serial: native USB — with deep sleep the console port disappears while the chip sleeps and returns when it wakes; 'serial port dropped' each cycle is expected (Listen only waits for it).

circuitpython.note: CircuitPython has no FireBeetle 2 ESP32-C5 build (checked 2026-10-24); the ESP32-C5-DevKitC-1-N8R8 build is the same module class and runs here, reporting espressif_esp32c5_devkitc_1_n8r8 — the same id the XIAO ESP32C5 reports, so the page keeps whichever of the two is selected. Pin names are the DevKit's IOxx. To verify on the board.
